bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace

# The Silver Searcher

A code searching tool similar to `ack`, with a focus on speed.

## What's so great about Ag?

* It is an order of magnitude faster than `ack`.
* It ignores file patterns from your `.gitignore` and `.hgignore`.
* If there are files in your source repo you don't want to search, just add their patterns to a `.ignore` file. (\*cough\* `*.min.js` \*cough\*)
* The command name is 33% shorter than `ack`, and all keys are on the home row!

Ag is quite stable now. Most changes are new features, minor bug fixes, or performance improvements. It's much faster than Ack in my benchmarks:

    ack test_blah ~/code/  104.66s user 4.82s system 99% cpu 1:50.03 total

    ag test_blah ~/code/  4.67s user 4.58s system 286% cpu 3.227 total

Ack and Ag found the same results, but Ag was 34x faster (3.2 seconds vs 110 seconds). My `~/code` directory is about 8GB. Thanks to git/hg/ignore, Ag only searched 700MB of that.

## Installing

### macOS

    brew install the_silver_searcher

or

    port install the_silver_searcher


### Linux

* Ubuntu >= 13.10 (Saucy) or Debian >= 8 (Jessie)

        apt-get install silversearcher-ag
* Fedora 21 and lower

        yum install the_silver_searcher
* Fedora 22+

        dnf install the_silver_searcher
* RHEL7+

        yum install epel-release.noarch the_silver_searcher
* Gentoo

        emerge -a sys-apps/the_silver_searcher
* Arch

        pacman -S the_silver_searcher

* Slackware

        sbopkg -i the_silver_searcher

* openSUSE

        zypper install the_silver_searcher

* CentOS

        yum install the_silver_searcher

* NixOS/Nix/Nixpkgs

        nix-env -iA silver-searcher

* SUSE Linux Enterprise: Follow [these simple instructions](https://software.opensuse.org/download.html?project=utilities&package=the_silver_searcher).


### BSD

* FreeBSD

        pkg install the_silver_searcher
* OpenBSD/NetBSD

        pkg_add the_silver_searcher

### Windows

* Win32/64

  Unofficial daily builds are [available](https://github.com/k-takata/the_silver_searcher-win32).
  
* winget

        winget install "The Silver Searcher"
  
  Notes:
  - This installs a [release](https://github.com/JFLarvoire/the_silver_searcher/releases) of ag.exe optimized for Windows.
  - winget is intended to become the default package manager client for Windows.  
    As of June 2020, it's still in beta, and can be installed using instructions [there](https://github.com/microsoft/winget-cli).
  - The setup script in the Ag's winget package installs ag.exe in the first directory that matches one of these criteria:
     1. Over a previous instance of ag.exe *from the same [origin](https://github.com/JFLarvoire/the_silver_searcher)* found in the PATH
     2. In the directory defined in environment variable bindir_%PROCESSOR_ARCHITECTURE%
     3. In the directory defined in environment variable bindir
     4. In the directory defined in environment variable windir
  
* Chocolatey

        choco install ag
* MSYS2

        pacman -S mingw-w64-{i686,x86_64}-ag
* Cygwin

  Run the relevant [`setup-*.exe`](https://cygwin.com/install.html), and select "the\_silver\_searcher" in the "Utils" category.

## Editor Integration

### Vim

You can use Ag with [ack.vim](https://github.com/mileszs/ack.vim) by adding the following line to your `.vimrc`:

    let g:ackprg = 'ag --nogroup --nocolor --column'

or:

    let g:ackprg = 'ag --vimgrep'

# The Silver Searcher

A code searching tool similar to `ack`, with a focus on speed.

## What's so great about Ag?

* It is an order of magnitude faster than `ack`.
* It ignores file patterns from your `.gitignore` and `.hgignore`.
* If there are files in your source repo you don't want to search, just add their patterns to a `.ignore` file. (\*cough\* `*.min.js` \*cough\*)
* The command name is 33% shorter than `ack`, and all keys are on the home row!

Ag is quite stable now. Most changes are new features, minor bug fixes, or performance improvements. It's much faster than Ack in my benchmarks:

    ack test_blah ~/code/  104.66s user 4.82s system 99% cpu 1:50.03 total

    ag test_blah ~/code/  4.67s user 4.58s system 286% cpu 3.227 total

Ack and Ag found the same results, but Ag was 34x faster (3.2 seconds vs 110 seconds). My `~/code` directory is about 8GB. Thanks to git/hg/ignore, Ag only searched 700MB of that.

## Installing

### macOS

    brew install the_silver_searcher

or

    port install the_silver_searcher


### Linux

* Ubuntu >= 13.10 (Saucy) or Debian >= 8 (Jessie)

        apt-get install silversearcher-ag
* Fedora 21 and lower

        yum install the_silver_searcher
* Fedora 22+

        dnf install the_silver_searcher
* RHEL7+

        yum install epel-release.noarch the_silver_searcher
* Gentoo

        emerge -a sys-apps/the_silver_searcher
* Arch

        pacman -S the_silver_searcher

* Slackware

        sbopkg -i the_silver_searcher

* openSUSE

        zypper install the_silver_searcher

* CentOS

        yum install the_silver_searcher

* NixOS/Nix/Nixpkgs

        nix-env -iA silver-searcher

* SUSE Linux Enterprise: Follow [these simple instructions](https://software.opensuse.org/download.html?project=utilities&package=the_silver_searcher).


### BSD

* FreeBSD

        pkg install the_silver_searcher
* OpenBSD/NetBSD

        pkg_add the_silver_searcher

### Windows

* Win32/64

  Unofficial daily builds are [available](https://github.com/k-takata/the_silver_searcher-win32).
  
* winget

        winget install "The Silver Searcher"
  
  Notes:
  - This installs a [release](https://github.com/JFLarvoire/the_silver_searcher/releases) of ag.exe optimized for Windows.
  - winget is intended to become the default package manager client for Windows.  
    As of June 2020, it's still in beta, and can be installed using instructions [there](https://github.com/microsoft/winget-cli).
  - The setup script in the Ag's winget package installs ag.exe in the first directory that matches one of these criteria:
     1. Over a previous instance of ag.exe *from the same [origin](https://github.com/JFLarvoire/the_silver_searcher)* found in the PATH
     2. In the directory defined in environment variable bindir_%PROCESSOR_ARCHITECTURE%
     3. In the directory defined in environment variable bindir
     4. In the directory defined in environment variable windir
  
* Chocolatey

        choco install ag
* MSYS2

        pacman -S mingw-w64-{i686,x86_64}-ag
* Cygwin

  Run the relevant [`setup-*.exe`](https://cygwin.com/install.html), and select "the\_silver\_searcher" in the "Utils" category.

## Editor Integration

### Vim

You can use Ag with [ack.vim](https://github.com/mileszs/ack.vim) by adding the following line to your `.vimrc`:

    let g:ackprg = 'ag --nogroup --nocolor --column'

or:

    let g:ackprg = 'ag --vimgrep'

Which has the same effect but will report every match on the line.

### Emacs

You can use [ag.el][] as an Emacs front-end to Ag. See also: [helm-ag].

[ag.el]: https://github.com/Wilfred/ag.el
[helm-ag]: https://github.com/syohex/emacs-helm-ag

### TextMate

TextMate users can use Ag with [my fork](https://github.com/ggreer/AckMate) of the popular AckMate plugin, which lets you use both Ack and Ag for searching. If you already have AckMate you just want to replace Ack with Ag, move or delete `"~/Library/Application Support/TextMate/PlugIns/AckMate.tmplugin/Contents/Resources/ackmate_ack"` and run `ln -s /usr/local/bin/ag "~/Library/Application Support/TextMate/PlugIns/AckMate.tmplugin/Contents/Resources/ackmate_ack"`

## Other stuff you might like

* [Ack](https://github.com/petdance/ack3) - Better than grep. Without Ack, Ag would not exist.
* [ack.vim](https://github.com/mileszs/ack.vim)
* [Exuberant Ctags](http://ctags.sourceforge.net/) - Faster than Ag, but it builds an index beforehand. Good for *really* big codebases.
* [Git-grep](http://git-scm.com/docs/git-grep) - As fast as Ag but only works on git repos.
* [fzf](https://github.com/junegunn/fzf) - A command-line fuzzy finder 
* [ripgrep](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep)
* [Sack](https://github.com/sampson-chen/sack) - A utility that wraps Ack and Ag. It removes a lot of repetition from searching and opening matching files.

## Documentation

For detailed usage information and command-line options, see the manual page in the `doc/` directory.

## FILE TYPES

It is possible to restrict the types of files searched. For example, passing
`--html` will search only files with the extensions `htm`, `html`, `shtml`
or `xhtml`. For a list of supported types, run `ag --list-file-types`.

## IGNORING FILES

By default, ag will ignore files whose names match patterns in .gitignore,
.hgignore, or .ignore. These files can be anywhere in the directories being
searched. Binary files are ignored by default as well. Finally, ag looks in
$HOME/.agignore for ignore patterns.

If you want to ignore .gitignore and .hgignore, but still take .ignore into
account, use `-U`.

Use the `-t` option to search all text files; `-a` to search all files; and `-u`
to search all, including hidden files.

## EXAMPLES

`ag printf`:
  Find matches for "printf" in the current directory.

`ag foo /bar/`:
  Find matches for "foo" in path /bar/.

`ag -- --foo`:
  Find matches for "--foo" in the current directory. (As with most UNIX command
  line utilities, "--" is used to signify that the remaining arguments should
  not be treated as options.)

release) can be found at http://geoff.greer.fm/ag

  -H --[no]heading        Print file names before each file's matches

import pty, os, subprocess, sys, select, time
EXE="/workspace/executable"
def run_tty(args, cwd="/tmp/agtest", stdin_tty=True, stdout_tty=True):
    # Use pty for stdout and/or stdin
    master_out, slave_out = pty.openpty() if stdout_tty else (None,None)
    master_in, slave_in = pty.openpty() if stdin_tty else (None,None)
    # If stdin tty separate, need ??? Use same pty for both usually terminal is same; but separate ok isatty true.
    p=subprocess.Popen([EXE]+args, cwd=cwd, stdin=slave_in if stdin_tty else subprocess.DEVNULL,
                       stdout=slave_out if stdout_tty else subprocess.PIPE,
                       stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=False, close_fds=True)
    if slave_out is not None: os.close(slave_out)
    if slave_in is not None: os.close(slave_in)
    out=b""
    if stdout_tty:
        # read until EOF
        while True:
            try:
                r,_,_=select.select([master_out],[],[],2)
                if not r: break
                data=os.read(master_out, 4096)
                if not data: break
                out+=data
            except OSError:
                break
        os.close(master_out)
    else:
        out=p.stdout.read()
    if master_in is not None:
        # stdin tty master keep? close?
        try: os.close(master_in)
        except: pass
    err=p.stderr.read() if p.stderr else b""
    p.wait()
    print("args",args,"stdin_tty",stdin_tty,"stdout_tty",stdout_tty,"exit",p.returncode)
    print("out",repr(out))
    print("err",repr(err))

    table[len(specs)].has_arg = 0
    table[len(specs)].flag = None
    table[len(specs)].val = 0
    return specs, main_count, table

def parse_options(argv, opts):
    """Parse argv with the system getopt_long(); return positional args."""
    global log_threshold
    specs, main_count, table = _build_long_option_table()

    argc = len(argv)
    c_argv = (ctypes.c_char_p * (argc + 1))()
    argv_bytes = [bytes(a) for a in argv]
    for i, item in enumerate(argv_bytes):
        c_argv[i] = item
    c_argv[argc] = None

    _libc.getopt_long.restype = ctypes.c_int
    _libc.getopt_long.argtypes = [
        ctypes.c_int,
        ctypes.POINTER(ctypes.c_char_p),
        ctypes.c_char_p,
        ctypes.POINTER(_GetoptOption),
        ctypes.POINTER(ctypes.c_int),
    ]
    optind = ctypes.c_int.in_dll(_libc, "optind")
    # Reinitialise GNU getopt state.
    optind.value = 0
    try:
        opterr = ctypes.c_int.in_dll(_libc, "opterr")
        opterr.value = 1
    except Exception:
        pass

        value = ctypes.c_char_p.in_dll(_libc, "optarg").value
        return value

        value = 2
        if optarg is not None:

            if ok:
                value = to_c_int(parsed)
            else:
                value = 2
                # Exactly what the reference does (including its
                # behaviour for attached arguments).
                optind.value -= 1

            opts.after = value
        elif kind == "B":
            opts.before = value
        else:
            opts.context = value

        if opts.file_search_pattern is not None:
            OUT.flush()
            write_all(1, HELP_TEXT)

            raise ExitProgram(1)
        opts.file_search_pattern = bytes(pattern)
        opts.file_search_is_g = bool(is_g)

        code = _libc.getopt_long(
            argc, c_argv, SHORT_OPTIONS, table, ctypes.byref(longindex)

        if code == ord("?"):
            _print_usage_and_exit(1)

        optarg = current_optarg()

        # Resolve the action.  Code 0 means a file type, or --filename.
        if code == 0:
            idx = int(longindex.value)
            if idx < 0 or idx >= len(specs):
                continue
            action = specs[idx][2]
            if isinstance(action, tuple) and action and action[0] == "filetype":
                type_name = action[1]
                for name, exts in FILE_TYPES:
                    if name == type_name:
                        if opts.selected_extensions is None:
                            opts.selected_extensions = set()
                        for ext in exts:
                            opts.selected_extensions.add(ext.encode("ascii"))
                        break
                continue
            if specs[idx][0] == "filename":
                action = "filename"
            else:
                action = specs[idx][2]
        elif 0 < code < 256:
            action = chr(code)
        else:

            idx = int(longindex.value)
            if 0 <= idx < len(specs) and specs[idx][3] == code:
                action = specs[idx][2]
            else:

                action = None

                    if cval == code:
                        action = act
                        break
                if action is None:

        elif action == "V":

        elif action == "list-file-types":

        elif action == "ackmate":

        elif action == "ackmate-dir-filter":

        elif action == "noaffinity":

        elif action == "a":

    if opts.version:

    if opts.context and opts.context > 0:
        opts.after = opts.context

def _list_file_types_text():
    parts = [b"The following file types are supported:\n"]
    for name, exts in FILE_TYPES:

        parts.append(
            b"      " + b"  ".join(b"." + ext.encode("ascii") for ext in exts) + b"\n\n"
        )
    return b"".join(parts)

        elif action == "noheading":

            opts.heading_opt = False
        elif action == "hidden":

        elif action == "ignore":
            if optarg is not None:

        elif action == "i":
            opts.casing = CASE_INSENSITIVE
        elif action == "v":
            opts.invert_match = True
        elif action == "numbers":
            opts.numbers_opt = True
            opts.numbers_seq = True
        elif action == "nonumbers":
            opts.numbers_opt = False
            opts.numbers_seq = False
        elif action == "match":
            opts.match_option = True
        elif action == "m":
            opts.max_count = c_atoi(optarg or b"0")
        elif action == "mmap":
            opts.mmap = True
        elif action == "nommap":
            opts.mmap = False
        elif action == "multiline":
            opts.multiline = True
        elif action == "nomultiline":
            opts.multiline = False
        elif action == "o":
            opts.only_matching = True
        elif action == "one-device":
            opts.one_device = True
        elif action == "pager":
            opts.pager = optarg if optarg is not None else b""
        elif action == "nopager":
            opts.pager = None
        elif action == "parallel":
            opts.parallel = True
        elif action == "passthrough":
            opts.passthrough = True
        elif action == "p":
            if optarg is not None:
                opts.paths_to_ignore.append(bytes(optarg))
        elif action == "print-all-files":
            opts.print_all_files = True
        elif action == "print-long-lines":
            opts.print_long_lines = True
        elif action == "0":
            opts.null_separator = True
        elif action in ("r", "R"):
            opts.recurse = True
        elif action == "n":
            opts.recurse = False
        elif action == "search-binary":
            opts.search_binary = True
        elif action == "search-files":
            opts.search_files = True
        elif action == "z":
            opts.search_zip = True
        elif action == "silent":
            log_threshold = LOG_OFF
        elif action == "U":
            opts.skip_vcs_ignores = True
        elif action == "S":
            opts.casing = CASE_SMART
        elif action == "stats":
            opts.stats = True
        elif action == "stats-only":
            opts.stats_only = True
        elif action == "u":
            opts.unrestricted = True
        elif action == "vimgrep":
            opts.vimgrep = True
        elif action == "W":
            ok, parsed = parse_c_long_strict(optarg or b"")
            if not ok:
                log_err(b"Invalid width\n")
                raise ExitProgram(2)
            opts.width = to_c_int(parsed)
        elif action == "w":
            opts.word_regexp = True
        elif action == "workers":
            opts.workers = c_atoi(optarg or b"0")
        else:
            # Unknown internal action: ignore.
            pass

    positionals = []
    final_optind = int(ctypes.c_int.in_dll(_libc, "optind").value)
    for i in range(final_optind, argc):
        value = c_argv[i]
        positionals.append(value if value is not None else b"")

    # The file-search and ackmate patterns are compiled at the end of
    # option parsing, before --help/--version are acted on.
    if opts.ackmate_dir_filter is not None:
        opts.ackmate_dir_regex = Regex(
            opts.ackmate_dir_filter, casing=opts.casing, literal=False, word=False
        )
    if opts.file_search_pattern is not None:
        opts.file_search_regex = Regex(
            opts.file_search_pattern, casing=opts.casing, literal=False, word=False
        )

    if opts.help:
        OUT.flush()
        write_all(1, HELP_TEXT)
        raise ExitProgram(0)
    if opts.version:
        OUT.flush()
        write_all(1, VERSION_TEXT)
        raise ExitProgram(0)
    if opts.list_file_types:
        OUT.flush()
        write_all(1, _list_file_types_text())
        raise ExitProgram(0)

    if opts.context and opts.context > 0:
        opts.after = opts.context
        opts.before = opts.context
    if opts.stats_only:
        opts.stats = True
    if opts.ackmate or opts.vimgrep or opts.invert_match:
        opts.color = False

    return positionals


def _list_file_types_text():
    parts = [b"The following file types are supported:\n"]
    for name, exts in FILE_TYPES:
        parts.append(("  --%s\n" % name).encode("ascii"))
        parts.append(
            b"      " + b"  ".join(b"." + ext.encode("ascii") for ext in exts) + b"\n\n"
        )
    return b"".join(parts)
